name: parametric-cad-design
title: Designing in Fusion
description: Use when designing or modelling in Fusion through the fusion-essentials tools - building a part, a surfaced product, an assembly, or a machining job, not running a fixed procedure. Rules are conditional strategies unless marked as a safety invariant; recipes demonstrate one construction with stated prerequisites, and their exemplars are examples, not requirements.
summary: Choose constructions by intended behavior and verify their effects. Recipes are worked examples: follow their dependencies, allowing companion reads, intermediate calls and justified alternatives.

sections.title: Kernel - every design
sections.use_when: always - the five habits that hold on every brief

rules.do: write what the design must satisfy and each interface as a checkable number - seating faces, aligned axes, clearance, wall thickness
rules.except: a throwaway probe

prove.observe: the active document, its units and what is already in it

rules.do: treat a sample sequence as one option; choose references and feature order for the interfaces and edits they must preserve
rules.except: a one-feature part with no downstream dependency

prove.observe: the relevant feature expressions and health after a representative intended edit
with trace=true, parameter-expression dependents; geometric references need separate checks

rules.do: share a dimension when values must track; keep independent decisions independent; name important drivers so later edits express intent
rules.except: a fixed reference whose source and role are stated

prove.observe: the intended expressions and their evaluated dimensions

rules.do: treat a successful call or healthy feature as partial evidence; check the actual effect against intent with relevant measurements and a useful view
rules.except: an effect already independently checked at this milestone

prove.observe: bounds and volume of the changed body and relevant neighbors

rules.do: compare the result with requirements and declared choices; distinguish what was created, computed, measured and tested from what remains unverified
rules.except: a disposable probe that makes no product claim

prove.observe: a view supporting the measured interfaces and intended form

sections.title: Plan
sections.use_when: before the first component exists - naming, variants, what is bought

rules.do: a made part takes a functional name, a bought part its spec - 'SS 6003 2RS (10 X 17 X 35mm)', 'SHCS M8 X 65mm' - so the browser is the bill of materials
rules.except: imported names

prove.observe: no 'Component1' and no 'Sketch1' left in the tree

rules.do: author them as configurations of one document driven by a few named parameters and a part-number property; check the active row before calling a failed compute a defect
rules.except: a single variant

prove.observe: the configuration table, its columns and the active row
body bounds of the active variant against its intended size

rules.example: the Configured Dumbbell: 14 rows varying weight_width, weight_length, weight_text and a Part Number

rules.when: a purchased, imported or generative body enters the design
rules.do: hold it as a base feature in its own component and re-cut only the interfaces on top of it with hole and chamfer features; never edit the frozen body
rules.except: a body you are modelling yourself

prove.observe: the imported definition and later interface features, as construction diagnostics
interface dimensions against their requirements
body bounds and volume against the expected interface modifications; these totals alone do not prove unchanged shape

sections.title: Sketch
sections.use_when: any profile that must survive a size change or drive a feature

rules.when: a profile has symmetry, equal spacing or a family of equal features
rules.do: draw the construction line, then constrain: symmetry about it, midpoint on it, equal between the members; dimensions pin only what remains
rules.except: a one-off reference sketch

prove.observe: the intended relations, evaluated dimensions and remaining freedom; test symmetry or spacing after a relevant edit

rules.example: a knife layout: 43 constraints, 5 dimensions; a handle profile: ten symmetry constraints, six expressions

rules.do: put the origin on a midpoint or at the crossing of two construction diagonals, never at a typed coordinate
rules.except: geometry projected from a body, which is already placed

prove.observe: a midpoint or coincident constraint naming the origin point

rules.do: type it once and write the other dimensions as that dimension's name (d239) or a named parameter
rules.except: two sizes that only happen to match today

prove.observe: dimension expressions referencing a name, not a repeated number

rules.when: an outline is a free curve
rules.do: draw a control-point spline and make its ends smooth to construction lines whose angles and lengths are dimensioned; the control polygon, not the curve, carries the intent
rules.except: a one-off path nothing else references, where a fit-point spline is enough

prove.observe: a cv_spline with 'smooth' constraints to lines that carry angle dimensions

rules.when: a clip, rib or pocket must follow an existing wall
rules.do: project the wall's edges into the sketch and dimension the detail by offset from them; projected geometry has no freedom, so few constraints fully constrain the sketch
rules.except: detail on a plane no body touches

prove.observe: projected references, evaluated offset dimensions and remaining freedom; full constraint is a diagnostic
the resulting detail offset from its supporting wall after a relevant edit

rules.when: a derived length or angle matters to the brief
rules.do: add it as a driven dimension and read it back; a master sketch may stay not fully constrained only where its free entities are the splines
rules.except: a sketch nobody will edit

prove.observe: dimensions with driving=false carrying the value the brief asked for

sections.title: Model
sections.use_when: turning sketches into a part - order, carving, patterns, threads, sheet metal, frozen bodies

rules.when: a moulded or cast part is built
rules.do: consider shaping and filleting the outer envelope before shelling, then adding interfaces; choose the order for the wall and edits you need
rules.except: geometry or dependencies better served by another order

prove.observe: the wall and interface dimensions after creation and a relevant size change

rules.when: the form is a block with a curved face or a tapered body
rules.do: extrude the block, loft or extrude the cutting form, split the block by it and remove the waste - the kept piece carries clean faces
rules.except: a form that is itself one extrude or revolve

prove.observe: one body left with the volume you expect after the split

rules.do: use a mirrored half when both sides must track, combining only a single physical part; otherwise express symmetry through suitable sketch or feature relationships
rules.except: features whose independent requirements merely produce a symmetric shape today

prove.observe: corresponding dimensions and positions remain symmetric after an intended change

rules.do: build one and pattern it; copies answering different requirements are modelled apart
rules.except: copies that merely share a shape

prove.observe: the repeated feature's definition
member dimensions and spacing after a relevant count or size change

rules.do: choose draft, walls, radii, holes and fit clearance from the intended process and interfaces; identify provisional values rather than borrowing sample dimensions
rules.except: an unsettled process, which is stated rather than assumed

prove.observe: the relevant face normals, radii and interfaces against the stated process requirements

rules.do: create a tapped hole with model_hole(tap=...); thread an existing cylindrical face with model_thread. Request modeled=true when helical geometry is required; reserve custom helices for a nonstandard form or a demonstrated capability gap
rules.except: a thread represented only as an explicitly labelled envelope

prove.observe: the Hole or Thread definition, designation and modeled state
mating dimensions of the claimed thread geometry

rules.do: read sheet_get for rules and sheet state; use sheet_create_flange for a base or edge flange, or sheet_convert for an existing uniform solid. sheet_create_flat_pattern creates a native flat, not verified development; inspect sheet_get(include=['features']) and the design_export cutting contours before fabrication
rules.except: a reference envelope with no fabrication claim

prove.observe: the applied rule, sheet bodies and flat-pattern state
the formed part's intended envelope

rules.when: bodies are still being carved out of one another
rules.do: stay in bodies until the part count settles, then promote each body to a named component before any joint
rules.except: a part known from the brief, which starts as its own component

prove.observe: named parts, their ownership and the intended joint relationships
the intended interface positions after a relevant edit

sections.title: Surface
sections.use_when: a shell, skin or product form that is not required to be manifold

rules.when: the outer form is the product
rules.do: consider surfaces when their sections and boundaries express the form well; stitch or thicken at boundaries that support the intended edits
rules.except: a solid or Form representation that better serves the same requirements

prove.observe: with tree_bodies=true, the selected body is_solid after relevant edits
body bounds against the intended dimensions

rules.do: provide enough intersection for the intended trim and possible edits; extend only when the existing cutter does not provide it
rules.except: a cutter that already overhangs

prove.observe: the retained body's bounds against the intended extent
retained face and edge locations; preservation beyond these observations remains unverified
the retained region against the intended boundary

rules.when: two skins must meet with a smooth transition
rules.do: consider split-and-loft or a radius-controlled fillet; choose the construction for the required continuity and shape controls
rules.except: a transition with no smoothness requirement

prove.observe: gap, normal angle and curvature jump sampled along the seam against the required continuity

rules.when: several parts share one outer form
rules.do: consider a shared master skin when several parts must follow the same form; choose same-document or derived ownership for the intended reuse and revision process
rules.except: independently designed forms that merely touch

prove.observe: the mating surfaces still agree after a shared-form change and update

rules.when: the quickest form is a solid but only some faces are wanted
rules.do: delete the faces you do not want; the remaining skin is the surface to build on
rules.except: a solid you will keep whole

prove.observe: the tree's body row reads is_solid false after the delete

sections.title: Assemble
sections.use_when: more than one component - how they are referenced, joined and moved

rules.do: choose relations for its actual freedoms and reference path; avoid duplicate constraints, while allowing independently organized subassemblies to use different constructions
rules.except: a placement study that makes no kinematic claim

prove.observe: the intended freedoms, health and component poses rather than a preferred joint count

rules.when: an assembly has a fixed moving mechanism
rules.do: establish one intentional reference path from the grounded part; do not ground parts to hide missing joints
rules.except: floating or multiple independent mechanisms

prove.observe: one ground_to_parent root and every joint reachable from it

rules.when: a part was modelled against its neighbours where it sits
rules.do: consider as-built joints to retain a deliberate placement; choose geometric joint references where they better express how interfaces must follow edits
rules.except: a static placement with no required joint relationship

prove.observe: the intended relative pose and motion limits
mating dimensions after relevant edits

rules.when: a joint needs a flip or an offset
rules.do: use the joint's align angle and align offset; do not add spacer bodies to fix a pose
rules.except: a real spacer part in the bill of materials

prove.observe: the joint's frame sits where the offset put it, and the occurrence list holds no spacer that is not a real part

rules.when: the mechanism has a driven joint
rules.do: drive it to home and a representative extreme; keep moving joints few, the rest rigid; link two joints with a motion link when one motion implies the other
rules.except: a joint with no travel of interest

prove.observe: the value at each pose
overlaps at each pose, intended fit or defect

rules.example: a nut overlapping a plain shaft is a thread modelled as a cylinder

rules.do: expect a set of adsk_ parameters per fastener and read only the authored set; name each fastener instance by its spec
rules.except: a design with no library parts

prove.observe: the authored user parameters are what comes back and generated_skipped counts the adsk_ ones the fasteners minted; include_generated=true lists those

sections.title: Validate
sections.use_when: the geometry exists and must be proved against the brief

rules.do: measure each and report the number - contact where parts engage, clearance where they move
rules.except: an interface the brief left open

prove.observe: the distance or angle at each interface

rules.do: read plane normals, axis directions and containment, then look: a flat stack passes every count while nothing nests, and a brick passes every measurement while looking nothing like the product
rules.except: a genuinely planar design

prove.observe: face normals and linear-edge directions
the silhouette reads as the object

rules.when: a measurement disagrees with the brief
rules.do: report the disagreement - a measurement is evidence about the artifact; intent comes from the brief
rules.except: a brief quoting a measured fact about existing hardware

prove.observe: the measured value beside the brief's

rules.do: confirm the effect through a read other than the tool's claim; read a refusal's reason before retrying
rules.except: a deferred write, confirmed through the poller it names

prove.observe: the affected design identity and state
the changed body's bounds and volume against the expected modelling effect

rules.do: leave the saved state valid, name the sketches and components, look at the result, and say what you could not do
rules.except: a scratch document

prove.observe: the document's save state

sections.title: Manufacture
sections.use_when: a machining job - setups, strategy choice, what a toolpath must prove

rules.do: hold the fixture as its own components beside the part, select only the part body as the model, and take the work coordinate system from the stock; the fixture is geometry the toolpaths must avoid, not decoration
rules.except: a setup sheet exercise with no fixture

prove.observe: selected_models names the part only and the wcs origin_mode is stated

rules.do: parallel skips steep areas by default and 3D contour skips shallow ones; machineSteepAreas and machineShallowAreas extend their coverage; consider scallop for both, choosing its stepover for the tool and required finish
rules.except: a flat part, where face and 2D contour suffice

prove.observe: the machineSteepAreas or machineShallowAreas difference in the pair
the coverage controls and tool carried by each operation
the intended operation is shown in isolation
visible passes on the intended regions

rules.example: a stepover of a tenth of the tool is a sample setting, not a universal finish requirement

rules.do: adaptive takes deep stepdowns at a light radial load and needs no leads or compensation; 2D pocket takes shallow stepdowns with a finishing pass and cutter compensation - pick adaptive for bulk removal, pocket when the wall finish comes from the same operation
rules.except: a slot, which wants the slot strategy on a closed slot contour

prove.observe: optimalLoad and maximumStepdown on adaptive; finishing passes and compensation on pocket
the geometry selections carried by each operation

rules.do: compare their geometry selections - chains, extension modes, stock contours, boundaries - because a parameter diff cannot see them
rules.except: operations that differ in parameters already

prove.observe: each operation's references: the chains and faces it was given

rules.when: a turning profile finishing cycle reports 'Lead-Out has been modified due to a gouge with the remaining stock'
rules.do: inspect the exit move and the stock the cycle leaves; turn the lead-out off, or leave allowance where a later pass removes it; regenerate and assess the result
rules.except: a cycle whose exit move has to clear a face, where the lead-out is the point

prove.observe: the warning after the change and whether the result is empty
the intended operation is shown in isolation
the exit path against the part and displayed stock

rules.example: measured on a turned flange: doLeadOut false, or useStockToLeave true with xStockToLeave and zStockToLeave at 0.5 mm, each cleared this warning

rules.when: a milling setup takes stock_mode 'previous_setup' after a turning setup
rules.do: MEASURED on a turned flange, one whole-model adaptive with its parameters untouched: it generated EMPTY on that setup under previous_setup stock in both the 'rest' and 'setupStockSilhouette' modes, and the same operation cut 347 s the moment the setup alone was switched to a relative box. These stock extents keep the relative-box numbers and describe nothing this setup cuts, so size a clearing strategy from the preceding setup's own operations, not from these extents. An operation's OWN rest is a separate knob: defineStockBy 'rest' reads restMaterialSource 'previousOperations' - the operations before it in THIS setup, not the setup's stock mode - and with every sibling valid it computes, no 'Failed to generate rest material.' among the warnings
rules.except: the first setup of a job, whose stock is the billet

prove.observe: the setup row reads stock_mode 'previous_setup' and stock_extents_describe says the box is not the stock
whether the clearing operation is named in empty_toolpaths - the list reports membership, never why

exemplar.access: Autodesk Design Samples; needs hub access, read only

recipes.title: Checking a generated cutting operation
recipes.use_when: a cutting operation expected to remove stock needs review before a demonstration post; machine release requires its own process checks

steps.do: read the operation, tool, selections, heights and stock source
steps.read_back: the actual settings and any freshness limits

steps.do: read state and emptiness
steps.read_back: the operation's computed state and whether it has a path

steps.do: read warnings and motion estimates
steps.read_back: time and distances; nonzero time alone does not prove stock removal

steps.do: show the operation alone
steps.read_back: the visibility selection

steps.do: inspect it against the feature, stock and fixture
steps.read_back: visible coverage and clearance; unseen collisions remain unverified

steps.do: post to the agreed output destination with the selected post
steps.read_back: the reported file path and size, or refusal

steps.do: re-read operation and program state
steps.read_back: the delivered scope and any outstanding warning or stale state

bar.measure: report computation, coverage evidence and output delivery separately; a nonempty file is not proof of controller suitability
bar.eyes: the isolated path agrees with measured feature positions and heights; disclose what the view cannot establish

recipes.title: Choosing a cross-hole approach
recipes.use_when: a known hole crosses a turned axis; decide through/blind intent, entry side, access and required depth before selecting a setup

steps.do: inspect the hole and available entry geometry
steps.read_back: the axis, position and relevant dimensions

steps.do: inspect the available setup frames
steps.read_back: whether an existing frame supports the intended approach

steps.do: create a dedicated setup only if the required approach needs one
steps.read_back: the intended model and setup identity

steps.do: bind the selected setup's orientation for that approach
steps.read_back: the bindings and available frame values

steps.do: create a drilling cycle with the appropriate tool
steps.read_back: the operation and tool

steps.do: select the intended hole faces
steps.read_back: the resolved faces

steps.do: set the required heights and drilling depth
steps.read_back: the actual height and depth settings

steps.do: generate and poll cam_get_status
steps.read_back: the actual completion state and warnings; change orientation only if the evidence requires it

steps.do: show the operation in isolation
steps.read_back: view_screenshot shows entry and depth against the measured hole

bar.measure: the generated approach and depth agree with the intended hole; through and blind cases have different acceptance
bar.eyes: the drill enters from the chosen side and reaches the specified depth
